The '''2017–18 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team''' represented [[Wichita State University]] in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They played their home games at [[Charles Koch Arena]] in [[Wichita, Kansas]] and are led by 11th-year head coach [[Gregg Marshall]]. The season marked the Shockers' first season as members of the [[American Athletic Conference]]. They finished the season 25–8, 14–4 in [[2017–18 American Athletic Conference men's basketball season|AAC play]] to finish a tie for second place. As the No. 2 seed in the [[2018 American Athletic Conference men's basketball tournament|AAC tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 Temple Owls men's basketball team|Temple]] in the quarterfinals before losing to [[2017–18 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]] in the semifinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the seventh season. As the No. 4 seed in the East region, they were upset in the first round by [[2017–18 Marshall Thundering Herd men's basketball team|Marshall]].

==Previous season==
The [[2016-17 Wichita State Shockers men's basketball team|Shockers]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 31–5, 17–1 to finish in a tie for first place in [[2016–17 Missouri Valley Conference men's basketball season|MVC play]]. In the [[2017 Missouri Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|MVC tournament]], they beat [[2016–17 Bradley Braves men's basketball team|Bradley]], [[2016–17 Missouri State Bears basketball team|Missouri State]], and [[2016–17 Illinois State Redbirds men's basketball team|Illinois State]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, they earned the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 10 seed in the South region (considered by everyone to be too high), they defeated No. 7 [[2016–17 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|Dayton]] in the first round before losing to No. 2 [[2016–17 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] in the second round.

The season marked the Shockers' final season as a member of the [[Missouri Valley Conference]] as the school announced on April 7, 2017 that it would be joining the American Athletic Conference effective July 1, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=American Athletic Conference votes unanimously to add Wichita State|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/19101126/american-athletic-conference-votes-add-wichita-state-shockers|website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

==Offseason==

===Returning players===
It was expected that the Shockers would return all five starters and nearly all of their scholarship players from the prior season. The only two seniors on the prior season's roster, Zach Bush and John Robert Simon, were [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-ons]]. Two underclass players, rising junior Eric Hamilton<ref name=Hamilton>{{cite news|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article141491354.html |title=Eric Hamilton will transfer from Wichita State’s basketball program |first=Paul |last=Suellentrop |newspaper=[[The Wichita Eagle]] |date=March 29, 2017 |accessdate=April 29, 2017}}</ref> and rising senior Daishon Smith,<ref name=Smith>{{cite news|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article145857684.html |title=Daishon Smith will transfer from Wichita State’s basketball team |first=Paul |last=Suellentrop |newspaper=The Wichita Eagle |date=April 20, 2017 |accessdate=April 29, 2017}}</ref> announced plans to transfer from Wichita State. Hamilton had been a little-used reserve;<ref name=Hamilton/> Smith had started at point guard at the beginning of the 2016–17 season, but lost his starting position to Landry Shamet and was seeing relatively little playing time by the end of the season.<ref name=Smith/>

Two other players, Markis McDuffie and Shaquille Morris, declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]], but neither hired an [[Sports agent|agent]], allowing them to return to Wichita State if they withdrew from the draft within 10 days of the end of the mid-May [[NBA Draft Combine]] (specifically May 24).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article146733139.html |title=Wichita State’s Morris, McDuffie continue NBA Draft process |first=Paul |last=Suellentrop |newspaper=The Wichita Eagle |date=April 25, 2017 |accessdate=April 26, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kansas.com/sports/college/wichita-state/article144877924.html|title=Wichita State’s McDuffie, Morris declare for NBA Draft |newspaper=The Wichita Eagle |accessdate=April 26, 2017}}</ref> Both withdrew from the draft the day before the deadline.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://thesunflower.com/18111/sports/morris-and-mcduffie-to-return-2017-2018-season/ |title=Morris and McDuffie to return 2017–2018 season |first=Aliyah |last=Funschelle |newspaper=The Sunflower |date=May 23, 2017 |accessdate=May 23, 2017}}</ref>

===Injuries===
On July 21, 2017, point guard [[Landry Shamet]], a potential All-American, suffered a stress fracture in his right foot and would need surgery.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/wichita-state-star-guard-landry-shamet-breaks-foot-surgery-scheduled-for-monday/|title=Wichita State star guard Landry Shamet breaks foot; surgery scheduled for Monday|work=CBSSports.com|access-date=2017-07-31|language=en}}</ref> He was expected to miss 12–16 weeks to recover from the injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/07/29/wichita-state-guard-landry-shamet-will-have-surgery-on-broken-foot/|title=Wichita State guard Landry Shamet will have surgery on broken foot|last=Phillips|first=Scott|date=2017-07-30|website=CollegeBasketballTalk|access-date=2017-07-31}}</ref> Shamet was expected to be ready for the team's season opener on November 10,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/wichita-state-landry-shamet-broken-foot-ncaa/b19dvnkqs0p114zjm9wwwt96z|title=Wichita State guard Landry Shamet suffers broken foot|date=2017-07-29|work=Sporting News|access-date=2017-07-31}}</ref> and that proved true, as he scored 17 points in only 17 minutes of action in the Shockers' 109–57 blowout of [[2017–18 UMKC Kangaroos men's basketball team|UMKC]] and, according to the [[Associated Press]], "looked completely recovered".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400987931 |title=No. 7 Wichita State blows past Missouri-Kansas City 109–57 |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN.com |date=November 10, 2017 |access-date=November 11, 2017}}</ref>

Shortly before practices began on September 29, it was announced that [[Markis McDuffie]] would be sidelined with a stress fracture in his left foot.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2017/09/25/report-wichita-states-mcduffie-out-with-stress-fracture/|title=Report: Wichita State’s McDuffie out with stress fracture|date=2017-09-26|work=CollegeBasketballTalk|access-date=2017-10-02|language=en-US}}</ref> It was expected that he would miss a majority of the non-conference schedule, but would return some time in late December.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://goshockers.com/news/2017/9/27/mens-basketball-trh-mcduffie-ready-to-get-recovery-started.aspx|title=TRH: McDuffie Ready to Get Recovery Started|website=Wichita State|language=en|access-date=2017-10-02}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kake.com/story/36480148/shockers-ready-to-step-up-in-shamets-and-mcduffies-absence|title=Shockers ready to step up in Shamet's and McDuffie's absence|last=Shannon|first=Chase|access-date=2017-10-02|language=en}}</ref> McDuffie returned for the final non-conference game on December 22 game against Florida Gulf Coast.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://thesunflower.com/23294/sports/mcduffie-returns-shockers-finish-non-conference-play-with-a-10-point-win-over-fgcu/|title=McDuffie returns; Shockers finish non-conference play with a 10-point win over FGCU – The Sunflower|last=Funschelle|first=Aliyah|website=thesunflower.com|language=en-US|access-date=2018-01-31}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kten.com/story/37130770/mcduffie-returns-as-the-no-11-shockers-rally-to-beat-fgcu|title=McDuffie returns as the No. 11 Shockers rally to beat FGCU|agency=Associated Press|access-date=2018-01-31|language=en}}</ref>

==Preseason==
At the conference's annual media day, the Shockers were narrowly picked to finish second in the AAC, receiving five of the 12 first place votes.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.theamerican.org/story.aspx?filename=mbb_1013171801&file_date=10/13/2017&path=mbball|title=Cincinnati Selected as 2017–18 American Men's Basketball Preseason Favorite|access-date=2017-10-24}}</ref> [[Landry Shamet]] was named to the preseason All-AAC first team.<ref name=":0" />
